newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: One dead, five hurt in Philippine ship fire - officials.
newsitem.headline: One dead, five hurt in Philippine ship fire - officials.

text.p: A ship with a leaking cargo of petroleum products burst into flames in Zamboanga City port on Saturday, killing a crewman and injuring five other people, crew members and officials said.

The fire that started at the 150-foot (46-metre) M/L Petron, which later sank, also damaged two other ships moored in the same port. Waiting passengers in the nearby terminal scampered to safety after hearing the explosions, port officials said.
Police said the dead victim was trapped inside his cabin while three of his colleagues had second-degree burns. Two other port labourers also suffered burns.
Six of the 10-man crew of M/L Petron were not hurt.

Zamboanga Bureau of Fire Protection director Felipe Carpio told reporters a vessel used for marine research by the Zamboanga State College of Marine Science and Technology and another foreign vessel, M/V Fortune Navigator, were also partially burned.
Other vessels in the Zamboanga port cleared the area after hearing explosions and as they saw thick smoke billowing from the cargo ship, said Zamboanga port manager Wilfredo Galvez.
The vessel was about to leave Zamboanga port for nearby Tawi-tawi island when it caught fire, its chief mechanic, Danny Bilangan, told reporters.
The burning vessel was towed 1.5 miles off the Zamboanga port, where it later sank, to prevent an oil spill to the shoreline, Galvez said.
Its cargo included 50,000 litres (11,000 gallons) of gasoline, 30,000 litres of kerosene, 20,000 litres of gas and 300 cylinders of liquified petroleum gas.
